verdict: Candidate A edges Candidate B, 26 of 28 against 22 of 28. Both understand the brief deeply and both ship solo-first, skippable journeys with honest limits, so product_understanding and ux_reasoning tie at 4, and both stop at 3 on interaction_completeness because neither packet evidences a single real flow state — Candidate A activates only default (2 of 12) while Candidate B's 4 of 12 reduce to a prototype-settings toast over an unchanged form. The pair separates on rendered quality: Candidate A's default captures are crisp and axe-clean at both viewports, whereas Candidate B fails its axe gate with 12 serious contrast violations (5 confirmed at each viewport by checks.json), ships washed-out flagship default captures, and shows a toast overlapping interface elements. Candidate A wins on accessibility (4 against 2) and on rendered hierarchy and judgment (4/4 against 3/3), despite its own visible 'Step 1 of 2' versus three-step-rail inconsistency and its failing accessible-names gate, which its wrapping labels and axe results contradict.
limitations: This is one blinded judge pass over static packets, not a statistical test and not proof of causation; I read only this pass's FILES.txt list, could not run either prototype interactively, relied on the supplied capture-report, checks and quality-gates reports for automated results, treated Candidate A's accessible-names gate failure as a probable harness limitation because the labels are present and two other checks pass (a judgment a stricter reader may reject), noted that Candidate B's washed-out default captures may partly be its entrance animation caught mid-fade rather than resting contrast (though checks.json still reports 5 serious violations per viewport), and did not test with assistive technology or beyond the captured viewports.
